title: Closed immersions descend along an fpqc covering of the target
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For each $i$, let $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ be the base change [def-pc-fibre-product] of $f$ along $g_i$. If every $f_i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then $f$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L6 (label lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion): the direction from all fpqc base changes to f

proof.text: Each $f_i$ is a closed immersion, hence affine by clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc]. Therefore $f$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine].

The affine morphism $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] applies with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and $i=0$ to each $g_i$, giving $g_i^*f_*\mathcal O_X\cong f_{i,*}\mathcal O_{X\times_YY_i}$. Since $f_i$ is a closed immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (1) says that $\mathcal O_{Y_i}\to f_{i,*}\mathcal O_{X\times_YY_i}$ is surjective. Given $y\in Y$, choose $i$ and $y_i\in Y_i$ over $y$. On stalks the base-change isomorphism identifies the tensor of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y$ with $\mathcal O_{Y_i,y_i}\to(f_{i,*}\mathcal O_{X\times_YY_i})_{y_i}$, hence this tensor map is surjective. The map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{Y_i,y_i}$ is a local homomorphism of local rings, and it is flat because $g_i$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], so the faithful-flat reflection statement [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective] makes $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y$ surjective.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L6, proof lines 5982-5998; the base-change input is Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 02KH

proof.text: By step 1 the morphism $f$ is affine, and by step 2 the map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y$ induced by $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ is surjective for every $y\in Y$. Hence $f$ is a closed immersion by [lem-pc-affine-surjective-structure-map-closed-immersion].
